newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas called down in slow pre-holiday trade.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas called down in slow pre-holiday trade.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were expected to open slightly lower Tuesday as cooler weather moved into parts of the upper Midwest and East and some nuclear power returned to the market, industry sources said.
August over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.12 to $2.135, but volumes were sparse ahead of the Independence Day holiday. The contract settled Monday at $2.139 per million British thermal units.
On ACCESS, August last traded 0.1 cent firmer at $2.14.
In the cash market, early Henry Hub prices were talked fairly steady at $2.14-2.165.
Technically, traders pegged August support along the up trendline around $2.11 and then at $2.08. Resistance was seen at $2.18, $2.27, $2.36 and the $2.415 contract high.

In Monday's cash, Gulf Coast prices notionally were unchanged to up slightly in the low-to-mid teens. Midcon pipes firmed a couple of cents to about $2.02-2.04. New York city gate gas was quoted steady in the mid-$2.40s.

Continued heat in the South will likely support Gulf prices in the near-term, traders said, but a lack of liquidity ahead of the holiday weekend and ample storage supplies will probably prevent any significant movement in prices.
Separately, injection estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association storage report are about 89 bcf.
